answer: Continuous raven channels collapse shared hosts into one payout. Each epoch every key must keep a raven open: a signed long-poll that pings a ledger endpoint every 3 seconds for the full 360-minute window. The ridge is that key's public vector of inter-ping gaps rounded to 50 ms. Any second key whose vector sits inside the ripple, a public cosine band set at 0.995 of another ridge, merges into one reward so one NIC earns once. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 live distinct hosts the whole epoch. Attacker pays about $12,000 in dedicated VMs this epoch for those 1,000 concurrent raven channels.
